newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia amends Constitution on land as EU demands.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia amends Constitution on land as EU demands.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament amended the constitution on Monday to allow foreigners to buy land, clearing the last barrier to ratification of the association agreement with the European Union.
The change was supported by 82 votes to two, and was widely expected after most parliamentary parties agreed on July 4 to change the constitution and ratify the association accord by July 15.

"The change will enable immediate ratification of the EU association accord and will fulfil a condition for Slovenia's future membership in the EU," Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek told parliament before the vote.
The parliament is expected to ratify the association accord on Tuesday, thus enabling the country to qualify for inclusion in the first round of EU expansion.

Last week, European Commission officials said ratification of the accord, which was signed in June last year, is a precondition for Slovenia to start negotiations on full membership in the EU in early 1998.

The vote followed a 10-hour debate, in which the opposition accused the government of poor negotiations with the European Union, necessitating the first change to the constitution adopted in 1991 when Slovenia declared independence from the former Yugoslavia.
